newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent falls, closes near low on MOC selling.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent falls, closes near low on MOC selling.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures fell sharply on Tuesday, ending near the day's low without any clear fundamental drivers, brokers said.
They said heavy market-on-close sell orders pulled the carpet from underneath prices, which had earlier found some support from Iraqi comments criticising the United States.
October Brent closed at $20.04 per barrel, 38 cents below Friday's settlement, having touched a high at $20.37.
"There was a lots of MOC selling, but there were no fresh headlines" a broker said.

Having opened lower, prices jumped in the middle of the day on comments by Iraq's deputy U.N. ambassador that the United States was hindering the implementation of an oil-for-food deal by insisting on too many monitors to supervise the plan.
But the United Nations said the deal, allowing Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil over six months to buy humanitarian supplies, was progressing nicely.
Dealers on the IPE floor said the late sell-off might be linked to traders' OTC positions and their desire to see a very low Brent reference price on Wednesday.
IPE September gas oil closed lower, but near the day's highs while Brent was still buoyed by the Iraqi story.
"It could be putting the (Iraqi) oil sales back further," one trader commented at the time.
September gas oil settled $1.75 per tonne softer at $189.25.
